Commentary.Commentary: ....Second innings...

England Women were expected to do well with the ball but were just not able to control the pace. Either too wayward or too inconsistent. However, they have the momentum now with a really good first hour from them. Lauren Bell and Sophie Ecclestone were the pick with three wickets each. England will now hope to bat long and score as much runs as possible till the end of the day.

So, a not was added on Day 2 by India and England will be really happy with how they started Day 2 as compared to Day 1. It was too inaccurate from England at the start and it cost them as India built partnerships one after the other. Apart from the openers, all of them chipped in. Fur batters fell in the 60s, Kaur missed out on her fifty by a run while Rana chipped in with 30 runs.

Hello and welcome to the action of Day 2 between India and England. The hosts dominated the proceedings after opting to bat first. Apart from the openers, top 7 batters made handy contributions with four fifty plus score while Kaur missed out her fifty by a run. The first thing England would like to do is take the remaining wickets quickly. They didn’t bowl well but could rectify by putting on a better show with the blade. Can England take the remaining wickets in the first session itself? Let’s find out.
...Day 2, Session 1...

It was a tough day for the English bowlers. Except for Filer who was almost the most expensive, all managed to get a wicket but itnwas a real struggle for them. England will hope to keep India under the 500-run mark and then bat well. An exciting Day two waits. Do join us for all the action. Until then, goodbye and take care.

A really good day for the Indians. It was a combined batting effort from them and they will be very pleased with their effort. Most of their batters got to decent scores. None went onto make a ton but a few half centuries has put them in a good spot. Sharma is playing well and she holds the key if they are wanting to cross the 500-run mark.

...Day 1, Session 2...

The final ball before lunch and England Women do not take their chance. That tells you how the session has gone so far for them. A bit off pace, bit inaccurate and a lot inconsistent with their line and length. England should and could do better with the ball. They are expected to do a lot better as this just helps Indian batters to settle in more and foreseen a big target. India on the other hand could not have asked for a better session. The openers gave a good start with some delightful boundaries on the card but both fell. It came down to two debutants to get things back on track and both have done unbelievably good. Satheesh Shubha is batting wonderfully, already bagged a fifty but she will look for more and so will Rodrigues. A lot to work for the English bowlers in the second session. Stay tuned.
